why:
The doc sentence is real, but the claimed consequence is false — this is the repo's canonical false positive: "the identifier really is unwired, but the consequence is false because something upstream already handled it."

1. DOC — CONFIRMED VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions.md` line 82: "`Bash(*)` is equivalent to `Bash` and matches all Bash commands. As a deny rule, both forms remove the tool from Claude's context." Not a paraphrase.

2. CITED FILES — the observations are individually true, and both are irrelevant to the claim.
   - `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/claude-permission-rules.ts:310` really does return `{ rule: { action, match: { kind: 'bash', pattern: specifier } } }`. But that raw matcher is compiled at `permission-dsl.ts:347` into `{ kind: 'bashPattern', pattern, action }` — the claim stops at the parser and never follows the compile step.
   - `permission-dsl.ts:900-905` really is `isWholeCapabilityDeniedByPermissionDsl`, and it really only inspects `rule.matcher.kind === 'tool'`. **But that function has ZERO production callers.** Repo-wide `rg -a 'isWholeCapabilityDeniedByPermissionDsl' . --glob '!node_modules'` returns only its own declaration, one comment reference at :977, and two assertions in `permission-dsl.test.ts:547-548`. It does not decide context removal. The claim named the wrong function.

3. ONE LAYER UP/DOWN — the behaviour is implemented, doc-cited in-code, and wired to the signed manifest.
   - The real decider is `isWholeToolDenyForIdentity` (`permission-dsl.ts:930`), whose `case 'bashPattern'` at :951-958 carries the exact quoted sentence as its comment and returns `matcher.pattern.trim() === '*' && identity.permissionName === 'Bash'`.
   - It is applied by `filterCapabilityIdentitiesByWholeToolDeny` (`permission-dsl.ts:972`), called in production at `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:1759`, whose result becomes `allowedBindingNames` on the manifest passed to `finalizePiExecutionManifest` — i.e. the tool is removed from the SIGNED manifest the subprocess advertises, not merely gated.
   - Positive control, both green (`bun test`, 22 pass / 0 fail / 116 expects): `permission-dsl.test.ts:484` asserts `kept('Bash')` and `kept('Bash(*)')` produce the identical surviving list while `kept('Bash(git *)')` keeps bash; and `packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/whole-tool-deny-manifest.test.ts:155` is an `it.each` row literally labelled `'the equivalent Bash(*) form'` that asserts the advertised manifest's `tools[].binding.piName` does NOT contain `bash` and that the gate still denies. Both halves of the doc sentence are enforced, and enforcement plus removal are asserted together so neither substitutes for the other.

4. THE PowerShell TAIL IS DOUBLY UNFOUNDED. The quoted context-removal sentence at :82 is Bash-specific; the PowerShell section at :235-237 says only "a bare `PowerShell` or `PowerShell(*)` matches every command" — it never claims context removal. And there is no PowerShell tool in this harness to remove: `rg -a "permissionName: 'PowerShell'" packages apps` returns nothing, and `harness-tool-descriptor.ts` has no `powershell` hit at all. PowerShell exists here only as a rule dialect (`claude-powershell-rule.ts`), not as an advertised tool.

Not an inert-worklist row and not a fork product difference — `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` has no `Bash(*)`/whole-tool entry. The only places this claim's text appears in the repo are the sweep documents that generated it: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-doc-sweep-phase1.md:38` and `docs/superpowers/specs/data/2026-07-31-doc-sweep-phase1.json`.
correctedState: Implemented and conformant. `Bash(*)` parses to `{ kind: 'bash', pattern: '*' }` (`claude-permission-rules.ts:310`) and compiles to `{ kind: 'bashPattern', pattern: '*' }` (`permission-dsl.ts:347`). Context removal is NOT decided by `isWholeCapabilityDeniedByPermissionDsl` — that function has no production caller. It is decided by `isWholeToolDenyForIdentity` (`permission-dsl.ts:930`), whose `case 'bashPattern'` at :951-958 quotes permissions.md:82 and treats a bare `*` pattern as a whole-tool deny (`matcher.pattern.trim() === '*' && identity.permissionName === 'Bash'`), while any narrower pattern stays a specifier that gates without removing. `filterCapabilityIdentitiesByWholeToolDeny` (:972) applies it in production at `pi-agent.ts:1759`, producing `allowedBindingNames` on the SIGNED execution manifest, so `deny: ["Bash(*)"]` and `deny: ["Bash"]` both drop the bash binding from what the model ever sees — and the gate independently denies, so removal never stands in for enforcement. Covered by `permission-dsl.test.ts:484` and `packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/whole-tool-deny-manifest.test.ts:155`; 22 pass / 0 fail. `PowerShell(*)` has no advertised PowerShell tool in this harness to remove, and permissions.md never claims PowerShell context removal.
